    if (!s) return false;

}

function isMachineNotice(comment) {

    if (typeof comment === 'string') return isMachineNoticeBody(comment);

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Rework input (`pr_discussions_raw.json`) includes the machine's own arming/status notices as review threads, so the rework agent spends replies on boilerplate responses to notices it (the harness) posted itself — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

**Root cause**: The discussion collector used by rework setup — `js/common/scm.js` `_createGithubProvider.fetchDiscussions()` (reached via `preCliReworkSetup.js` → `gh.fetchDiscussionsAndRawData(scm, …)` → SCM-object delegation) — copies **every** conversation returned by `github_get_pr_conversations` into `rawThreads` and the markdown with **no machine-notice filtering at all**. The back-compat string path in `js/common/githubHelpers.js` `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData()` only filters `[bot]`-suffixed authors (`BOT_AUTHORS`), but the harness's own machine identity (e.g. `ai-teammate`) is a normal login; its notices — arming notices (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed.`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, `🅿️→▶ validation_failed cleared…`), run/CI status posts (`🔁 Cancelled required checks re-run`, `⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head`, `⚠️ Merge conflict with main`, `🛑 …needs a human`), rework results (`✅/⚠️/❌ Rework …`, `## 🔧 Rework Complete —`, `✅ Addressed…`) and review-result posts (`🔍 Automated PR Review Completed`) — pass the filter. Those notices land in `pr_discussions_raw.json` as threads with reply targeting, and the agent dutifully replies to each.

**Impact**: Every rework leg on a PR carrying machine notices wastes replies (token burn, PR comment spam) and can report "all threads addressed" while real reviewer threads go unanswered; `review_state.md`'s open-thread inventory is inflated the same way.

**Fix approach**: Marker-keyed classification, not fuzzy text matching or authorship alone (the reviewer identity in this harness IS the machine login, so authorship cannot discriminate). New shared module `js/common/machineNotice.js` owns the exact marker strings the harness posts (single source of truth, anchored at body start after stripping a markdown heading prefix, so a reviewer comment merely *quoting* a notice is not filtered). Wire it into both `fetchDiscussions` implementations: machine-notice conversations are dropped from `rawThreads` and excluded from the markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads). `preCliReworkSetup.buildReviewStateMd` then sees only real threads. The gh-799 fallback already covers AC3: with zero real threads, `ensureInputContextContract` writes the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder and `review_state.md` carries the verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED warning included), so the agent works from the verdict with `threadId:null` honesty preserved in `pushReworkChanges`.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix for gh-808.

**Non-goals respected**: notice text/format posted by the armer unchanged (filter side only); review-verdict semantics (#807) untouched; GitLab/ADO providers untouched (the arming notices are posted via `github_create_comment`, GitHub-only surface).
"}

{"path":"outputs/rca.md","content":"# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: Rework input (`pr_discussions_raw.json`) includes the machine's own arming/status notices as review threads, so the rework agent spends replies on boilerplate responses to notices it (the harness) posted itself — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

**Root cause**: The discussion collector used by rework setup — `js/common/scm.js` `_createGithubProvider.fetchDiscussions()` (reached via `preCliReworkSetup.js` → `gh.fetchDiscussionsAndRawData(scm, …)` → SCM-object delegation) — copies **every** conversation returned by `github_get_pr_conversations` into `rawThreads` and the markdown with **no machine-notice filtering at all**. The back-compat string path in `js/common/githubHelpers.js` `fetchDiscussionsAndRawData()` only filters `[bot]`-suffixed authors (`BOT_AUTHORS`), but the harness's own machine identity (e.g. `ai-teammate`) is a normal login; its notices — arming notices (`🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed.`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, `🅿️→▶ validation_failed cleared…`), run/CI status posts (`🔁 Cancelled required checks re-run`, `⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head`, `⚠️ Merge conflict with main`, `🛑 …needs a human`), rework results (`✅/⚠️/❌ Rework …`, `## 🔧 Rework Complete —`, `✅ Addressed…`) and review-result posts (`🔍 Automated PR Review Completed`) — pass the filter. Those notices land in `pr_discussions_raw.json` as threads with reply targeting, and the agent dutifully replies to each.

**Impact**: Every rework leg on a PR carrying machine notices wastes replies (token burn, PR comment spam) and can report "all threads addressed" while real reviewer threads go unanswered; `review_state.md`'s open-thread inventory is inflated the same way.

**Fix approach**: Marker-keyed classification, not fuzzy text matching or authorship alone (the reviewer identity in this harness IS the machine login, so authorship cannot discriminate). New shared module `js/common/machineNotice.js` owns the exact marker strings the harness posts (single source of truth, anchored at body start after stripping a markdown heading prefix, so a reviewer comment merely *quoting* a notice is not filtered). Wire it into both `fetchDiscussions` implementations: machine-notice conversations are dropped from `rawThreads` and excluded from the markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads). `preCliReworkSetup.buildReviewStateMd` then sees only real threads. The gh-799 fallback already covers AC3: with zero real threads, `ensureInputContextContract` writes the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder and `review_state.md` carries the verdict (CHANGES_REQUESTED warning included), so the agent works from the verdict with `threadId:null` honesty preserved in `pushReworkChanges`.

**Previous attempt**: N/A — first fix for gh-808.

**Non-goals respected**: notice text/format posted by the armer unchanged (filter side only); review-verdict semantics (#807) untouched; GitLab/ADO providers untouched (the arming notices are posted via `github_create_comment`, GitHub-only surface).
"}

var MACHINE_NOTICE_MARKERS = [ ... ];  // exact harness strings

function stripLeadingHeading(text) {
    var s = String(text || '').replace(/^\s+/, '');

function isMachineNoticeBody(body) {

function isMachineNotice(comment) {

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. ### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. - `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.

RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. {"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. {"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

{"content":"### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. The harness's own machine login (a normal user account) posts arming/status notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries), so the rework agent saw them as review threads with reply targeting and spent its replies on boilerplate — 9 of 13 replies on fa PR #1428 round 2.

### Fix

- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new): single source of truth for machine-notice classification — anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers the harness posters write (`smAgent.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`, `postPRReviewComments.js`), with a leading markdown-heading strip. A reviewer comment that merely quotes a notice never matches. Also owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js`: GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `rawThreads` and the discussions markdown (with an exclusion note, same pattern as resolved threads) and now applies the bot flag/exclusion the string path already had.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js`: string path drops notices entirely (AC1) instead of leaking them; bot handling unchanged; exclusion note + counters extended.
- No changes to notice texts posted by the armer (filter side only, per ticket non-goals); GitLab/ADO providers untouched (arming notices are GitHub-only via `github_create_comment`).

### Test Coverage

- `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` (new, 14 tests): L1 classifier (notice vs real thread vs reviewer-quoting-a-notice edge), L2 replay of the #1428-shaped 13-comment corpus through both collection paths — exactly the 4 real threads survive with `threadId`s intact (gh-799 contract, AC2) and zero notice entries remain (AC1) — plus the AC3 fallback: notices-only PR collapses to the `{"threads":[]}` placeholder while `review_state.md` still carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict summary. RED first (13 failures pre-fix), GREEN after.
- Full suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` — all suites pass, 0 failures.

### Notes

- AC4 (live check: next rework leg's reply count == real thread count) requires a live rework cycle; the filter makes the input deterministic so the check reduces to counting real threads.
- `threadId:null` honesty in agent output remains governed by pushReworkChanges (gh-799), unchanged.

### Root Cause

Rework setup collected PR discussions with no machine-notice filtering: the GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (`js/common/scm.js`) copied every conversation into `pr_discussions_raw.json`, and the string-arg path (`js/common/githubHelpers.js`) only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts. All done. Final state verified — full suite green, outputs in place at the job root.

## Summary

**Bug (gh-808)**: Rework input fed the machine's own arming/status notices back as review threads — the rework agent spent 9 of 13 replies (fa PR #1428 round 2) on boilerplate answers to the harness's own notices.

**Root cause**: The GitHub SCM provider's `fetchDiscussions` (the path `preCliReworkSetup.js` actually uses) had **no notice filtering at all**, and the string-arg path in `githubHelpers.js` only filtered `[bot]`-suffixed accounts — the machine login (e.g. `ai-teammate`) is a normal user, so its arming notices (`🧵 …rework armed`, `🅿️ Validation red — PR parked`, validation/re-run reports, rework/review summaries) passed through as reply-targetable threads.

**Fix (TDD: RED 13 failures → GREEN → full suite 1988/0)**:
- `js/common/machineNotice.js` (new) — single source of truth: anchored, marker-keyed match on the exact body-start markers each harness poster writes (heading-prefix stripped); a reviewer comment merely *quoting* a notice never matches; owns the shared `[bot]`-author heuristic.
- `js/common/scm.js` — GitHub provider drops notice conversations from `pr_discussions_raw.json` and the markdown (AC1), now also flags/excludes bot threads.
- `js/common/githubHelpers.js` — string path drops notices entirely (was: leaked into rawThreads); bot behavior preserved.
- AC2 verified (4 real corpus threads survive with `threadId`s intact — gh-799 contract); AC3 verified end-to-end (notices-only PR → `{"threads":[]}` placeholder + `review_state.md` carries the CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict).
- Test harness require-maps updated where real `scm.js`/`githubHelpers.js` are loaded (7 files).

**Deliverables**: `outputs/rca.md`, `outputs/response.md` (PR description), `js/unit-tests/test_machineNotice.js` + `run_machineNotice.json` (registered in `run_all.json`). AC4 (live reply-count check) noted for the next rework cycle.
